title: API Surface PRD: Generation + Embeddings + Rerank Behavioral Guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description: Context: We need a single PRD that defines behavioral guardrails and operational acceptance for the hosted API family we ship to customers: chat (conversational API), completions (single-turn generation), embeddings, and rerank. This ticket consolidates requirements that ensure stability, backward-compatible behavior, quality signal plumbing, and a deterministic rollout strategy to meet SLOs + cost targets. Goals: 1) Define minimal behavioral contracts for generation and chat (stop tokens, default temperature ladder, function-calling semantics for chat), 2) Specify embedding API stability (vector dimensionality guarantees, stable normalization), 3) Rerank endpoint scoring contract and latency bounds, 4) Acceptance criteria and launch checklist focusing on reliability, observability, and rollback conditions. Out of scope: model architecture changes, on-prem/private deployment packaging (those are separate PRDs).
acceptance_criteria: Generation and Chat: Default response behavior documented and validated by automated conformance suite (deterministic tokenization boundary tests, stop-sequence behavior across top-3 models)
Function-calling: schema validation test pass with 10 canonical schema samples; fallback path returns well-formed assistant message when function call is unsupported
Streaming: SSE/HTTP2 streaming handshake works end-to-end in SDKs; no more than 5% of streams fail to reconnect under simulated 99th percentile latency spikes
Embeddings: Dimension and L2 normalization guarantees enforced; embedding drift test (1000-sample stability check between model patch versions) shows <0.5 cosine change for stable seed prompts
Rerank: Score monotonicity property for pairwise swaps verified in unit tests; P95 latency for rerank (up to 10 items) < 120ms in hosted standard tier
SLOs: API-level P95 latency for generation under normal load < 250ms per token; error rate <0.5% over a 24h window in canary; throttles and quotas enforce per-account limits
Observability: Token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency histograms, and per-route error dashboards populated and linked in Console prior to staged rollout
Fallbacks: Policy that maps degraded models to compatible family variants defined and exercised in simulated capacity failure scenario
Billing: Metering hook validated to record tokens and embedding units identical to production billing logic in two independent tests
Security: No customer PII persists in hosted logs for requests flagged as ephemeral; KMS-integrated keys optional but tested for Dedicated flow

Implement and merge conformance test suite (GH PR linked) and green for all models in catalog
Create console dashboards: per-route latency, token cost, error reason breakdowns (links below)
Run loadtest simulating 3 tenant profiles: low-burst, mid-sustained, enterprise commit pattern; collect cost and latency regressions
Validate canary rollout automation: percent steps, escalation hooks, auto-rollback on kill conditions
Run billing reconciliation job for dev tenant and sample customers to ensure tokens and embedding units align
Complete security questionnaire and ensure ephemeral log flagging works for hosted tier
Update API docs + SDK patches for function-calling schema and streaming changes
Customer-facing changelog entry drafted and approved by Communications
Schedule support on-call and runbook distribution to CS/SE teams for the first 2 weeks after launch
Tag release and deploy to staging -> canary -> regional rollout per rollout plan

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model patch causes embedding drift affecting downstream similarity tasks. Mitigation: embedding drift gate in canary and automatic rollback if drift exceeds threshold
Risk: Rerank scoring non-determinism due to GPU kernel changes. Mitigation: add deterministic scoring path and pairwise unit tests; block launch until stable
Risk: Streaming reconnection behaviors differ across SDKs. Mitigation: ship SDK fixes and mark legacy SDK versions as incompatible in release notes
Risk: Unexpected cost increases from batching changes. Mitigation: run cost-sensitivity loadtests and add per-customer burst caps
rollout_plan: Canary step 1: 0.5% traffic (internal beta tenants) for 24h; evaluate SLOs and cost signals
Canary step 2: 5% traffic (opt-in customers) for 48h; automated checks: error rate <0.5%, embedding drift <0.5 cosine, rerank P95 <120ms
Ramp: 25% for 72h if canary checks green, then 60% for 24h
Kill conditions: sustained error rate increase +0.25pp over baseline for 30m, embedding drift >0.5 cosine, or billing discrepancy >2%
Emergency rollback: immediate routing to prior stable model family and notify on-call and PM
